newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Growing dissent among Creditanstalt bidders - paper.
newsitem.headline: Growing dissent among Creditanstalt bidders - paper.

text.p: A consortium of bidders for the Austrian government's sell-off candidate Creditanstalt was deeply split over savings bank Die Erste's plans for setting up a joint holding company with the bank, daily Kurier reported on Monday.
Die Erste Oesterreichische Spar-Casse Bank AG has proposed to set up a holding with Creditanstalt-Bankverein which would hold 74.9 percent of Die Erste's shares and all of Creditanstalt's.

Its consortium partners, including Germany's Commerzbank AG and Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali have voiced increasing concern about the proposed holding structure and the weight Die Erste would carry in it.
Representatives of Commerzbank had threatened to leave the consortium and submit their own bid for the Austrian government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt, Kurier said.
Independent confirmation for the reports was not immediately available.

Die Erste on Friday said agreement over a final bid for Austria's number two bank was still a long way off and said it had proposed to increase its weight in the planned holding by offering an additional, unspecified amount of cash.

The savings bank, together with its partners, is the only known bidder for Creditanstalt, which has been on the government's sell-off list for more than six years. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
